div.l: There as this lord / was kepere of the selle
The reule of seynt Mavr / othir of seynt Benyt
Be cause it was old / and somdel streyht
This ilke monk / leet olde thynges pace
And helde After / the newe world the trace
He yaf nat of the tixt / a pulled henne
That sayth that hunterys / beth nat holy menne
Ne that a monke / whan he is recheles
Is likned to a fissh / that is waterles
This is to seyne / a monk out of his cloistre
But thilke tixt / helde he nat worth an oystre
And I seyde / his opynyoıı̄un was good
What shulde he studie / and make hym self wood .
Vp on a boke in cloistre / al day to povre
And swynke / with his handes and laboure
As Austyn̄ bit / how shuld the world be ʆser ved ·
Lat Austyn̄ have his swink / to hym reʆserved ·
Therfor· he was / a pⁱrikasowr a ryht
Grehoıı̄undes he hadde / as swyft as fowle in flight
Of pⁱrikyng and of huntyng / for the hare
Was al his lust / for no cost wolde he spare
I saw his sleves purfylyd at the honde
With grys / and that the fynest in a londe
And forto fastene / his hood vndyr the chyn ·
He had of gold / wrowht a wol coryows pyn
A lowe knotte in the grettere / ther was
His hed was balled / that shon as any glas ·
And eke his face / as he hadde be a noynt
He was a lorde wel fat / and in good poynt
His eyen stepe / and rollyng / in his hed
That stemed / as a forneys of a leed ·
His botis souple / his hors in greet astat
Now certeynly / he was a Fayr prelat
